# Critique — Pattern 8 (Substances)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Tobacco & Nicotine (~10%), Alcohol Use & Recovery (~15%), Cannabis & Other Substances (~20%), Treatment & Harm Reduction (~20%), and lifestyle/monitoring fillers (~35%). Questions regarding recreational drug use and prescription controlled substances carried potential self-incrimination risks. To draw a safe line, we restricted current illicit drug use questions to broad categories (e.g., "Have you ever used stimulants recreationally?") and focused specifically on legal or medically managed contexts, such as opioid prescriptions or medication-assisted treatment. Overlaps exist with the Mental Health and Cardiovascular domains (e.g., family history of substance use, tobacco smoking) because addiction is a psychiatric condition with extreme vascular and lung-health impacts. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions representing protective actions, recovery milestones, and harm-reduction readiness (e.g., carrying naloxone, being in recovery, attending AA, nicotine cessation attempts). We paraphrased standard screening concepts from AUDIT and CAGE without reproducing items verbatim. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your substance symptoms weekly...") as weekly logging is highly uncommon and carries low clinical validation compared to established screening instruments.
